slides.h: The knocker-up was a human alarm clock.
slides.p: Before cheap alarm clocks, British workers paid them to tap on bedroom windows with long poles. In London, Mary Smith used a pea shooter.

slides.h: "Computer" used to be a person's job title.
slides.p: Rooms of human computers did math by hand. At NASA, John Glenn asked Katherine Johnson to check the machine's numbers before his 1962 orbit.
Kids reset every pin by hand, often late at night, dodging flying pins. Automatic pinsetters took over in the 1950s.

slides.h: Ice was cut from frozen lakes and shipped across the world.
slides.p: Boston's "Ice King" Frederic Tudor sent New England ice to the Caribbean and, in 1833, all the way to India.
